newsitem.title: USA: PETsMART down on comp sale, earnings fears.
newsitem.headline: PETsMART down on comp sale, earnings fears.

text.p: Shares of PETsMART Inc dropped nearly 25 percent Friday after Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette downgraded the stock, adding to the market's concern about same-store sales and earnings, analysts said.
Shares of the pet supply retailer dropped 3-15/16 to 12 at midday Friday. PETsMart was the second most-heavily traded Nasdaq issue.
DLJ downgraded the stock to a buy and removed it from its recommended list. Additional details were not immediately available.
That move magnified investors' concerns that same-store sales for the first quarter and the year may be weaker than expected, analysts said.

Some Wall Street analysts previously had expected PETsMART to post double-digit same store sales growth of about 10-12 percent. But due to some softness in areas such as flea and tick products, some industry analysts now expert the retailer to post high single-digit comparable sales.
PETsMART did not return calls seeking comment.

One analyst suggested that PETsMART's management has been distracted with recent acquisitions and expansions. PETsMART recently merged with British pet store operator Pet City Holdings Plc and has made forays into the horse supplies and services market.
"People are thinking that the company needs to spend a little less time on deal-making and more time on the nuts and bolts of the business," said Otto Grote, a retail analyst with Derby Securities.
"Stock holders have seen earnings evaporate due to restructure costs, acquisitions costs. Somewhere along the line we have to see some real earnings," Grote said.
For the fiscal year ending January 1998, analysts expect PETsMART to earn $0.61 a share, compared with $0.43 a share for fiscal 1997, according to First Call.
Although investors are disappointed by the company's near-term comparable sales prospects, some analysts said PETsMART's long-term potential remains strong.
PETsMART, which has seen its stock drop about 45 percent since the end of 1996, remains a buy at these levels, analysts said.
